title: Environment-aware deployment matrix for canary, A/B and shadow rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We need deterministic, auditable rollout semantics for model version changes that behave consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but also respect environment-specific constraints (network egress policies, KMS/HSM access, maintenance windows, GPU pool sizing). Current gap: ad-hoc translation of rollout configs causes behavioral drift (e.g., a Hosted canary with short TTLs and automatic KV warmup works, but the same config silently underperforms in Private due to restricted image download timing and disabled autoscaling).

Goals: Standardized deployment matrix + translation layer that: (1) defines canonical canary/A-B/shadow primitives and mappings to each environment; (2) provides safe defaults for cache warming, traffic ramp cadence, and rollback triggers; (3) surfaces environment constraints at planning time; (4) supports automatic rollback based on mixed signal metrics (latency P95, token error rate, hallucination score from quality evals, and cost spike thresholds).

Design summary:
- Canonical primitives: Canary(percent, duration, prefilling_strategy), AB(variants, split_policy, metrics), Shadow(target, sampling_rate, async_observe). These are the product-level API configs that teams will use.
- Translation layer: runtime-config-translator maps canonical primitives to environment-specific plans. Examples: Hosted => short TTL KV cache, fast autoscale-on-demand; Dedicated => pin to reserved GPU pool with ramp controls; Private => require pre-uploaded model artifact, schedule during maintenance window, disable automated node provisioning.
- Prefilling / cache-warming: Implement pre-warming hooks that can run synthetic prefix traffic (configurable OR disabled for Private). The translator enforces a prefilling_strategy fallback to "no-op" if environment lacks external traffic generators.
- Metrics and rollback: Define a scoring function composed of normalized latency delta, SLO error rate delta, quality regression from eval-set (text-sim or BLEU-like), and cost per-token delta. If score > configured threshold for duration T, trigger auto-rollback. For Private deployments, auto-rollback defaults to "alert + manual approval" unless operator enables automatic rollbacks.
- Safety controls: max-rollout-percent cap per env, hard circuit-breakers for KMS failures, and explicit approval gates for artifacts with new quantization formats or kernel-level changes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict parity vs safety: Forcing identical behavior across envs increases developer predictability but risks unsafe actions in constrained Private clusters. We implement parity at the API surface while intentionally allowing safe divergences at translation time (documented and visible in the Console).
- Automated rollback aggressiveness: Aggressive rollbacks reduce customer impact but increase churn and false positives. We propose a two-tier policy: fast rollback for catastrophic failures (panics, out-of-memory, high error rate) and conservative rollback for quality regressions requiring ensemble signals.
- Prefill cost: Synthetic pre-warming reduces first-user latency but increases token cost. We provide a cost-budget parameter and recommend enabling only for canaries < 5% traffic in Hosted/Dedicated.

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) Spec and policy matrix (this ticket) — design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deployment+Matrix+Spec
2) Translator PoC (service + unit tests) that emits environment plans (ENG-PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4882) — target branch landed by 2026-03-05.
3) Metric scoring library and observability hooks (Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rollouts/regression) — integration tests + synthetic replay harness.
4) Console UX for visible plan diffs and approval flows (design: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xYcExampleDesign)
5) E2E smoke tests across Hosted, Dedicated, Private (staging clusters).

Acceptance criteria: Canonical API implemented, translator returns documented plan for each environment, automatic rollback firing in Hosted/Dedicated for synthetic regression scenarios, Console shows plan diffs and required approvals for Private, and at least two customer teams validate canary->full rollout with rollback semantics.

Notes on environment constraints: Private environments commonly enforce (a) artifact pre-staging, (b) no external egress for downloading monitoring sidecars, (c) stricter RBAC for rollbacks, and (d) longer maintenance windows. Translator must be able to mark actions as "operator-required".
